engagement_title: Nimbadesk launch quarter: bring a year of mixed screenshots and an AI-made logo to one product, then ship the sell sheets, the pitch deck, the launch social and the booth badge run
vertical: Technology, SaaS and startups: B2B help desk software sold per seat to IT and operations leads at fifty to five hundred person firms (Denver, Colorado)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork collateral post quoted verbatim in the ledger's grounding_note, which specifies "DELIVERABLE 2 - One-Page Service Overview: single/double-sided 8.5\"x11\" sell sheet" carrying a "header with branding and compelling title", a "company advantage" section, "core-services bullets" and "a prominent CTA", laid out on "clean grids", with the whole set required to "feel clean, modern, trustworthy and polished, referencing the website's palette/typography". The original poster was a legal and MVA case management firm; it is laundered here to the coined, IP clean B2B SaaS company Nimbadesk (nimbus plus desk), which names no real help desk product. Co-anchor: the Upwork post from a founder whose logo was "created on AI" and who needed it turned into a "vector file so it can be used in multiple platforms" and kept "high-quality across different formats", laundered from that brief's startup to the same fictional company. The ledger's verdict is STRENGTHEN, and the concept is kept whole: it previously sat almost entirely on one authoring surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the honest fuller commission runnable, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, a raster mark can be traced into placeable vector geometry, and a printer's badge PDF can be reverse engineered into a genuine variable data run. So this is what that client actually needed in one engagement: the sell sheets they specified, the deck and the launch set the same launch requires, the mark recovered from the only file that exists, and the fourteen booth badges the conference needs, all editable because pricing moves every quarter.
client_one_liner: Build our launch collateral from the product screenshots and the logo we have, the sell sheets, the pitch deck, the launch social and the booth badges, all editable and all reading as one product.
client_brief:
Nimbadesk, launch quarter

We are eleven people in Denver. Nimbadesk is help desk software for IT and operations teams at companies of fifty to five hundred people. We have been in private beta for fourteen months with thirty one paying accounts. In February three things land in the same three weeks: sign ups open, we present to a seed extension round, and we work a ten by ten booth at a mid market IT operations conference in Chicago.

What we have. Screenshots of the product, taken across the year by whoever happened to be at a keyboard. A logo our first designer generated with an AI tool and sent us as a picture, which is the only version that exists anywhere. Headshots of the booth team taken in our own office. A metrics file with the numbers our chief executive wants on a chart. Pricing and copy as approved by us.

What we need. Three sell sheets, one per feature, the thing sales attaches to an email and prints for a meeting. A pitch deck that runs from the problem through the product, the metrics, how teams work today, our three tiers as a table a person can actually read, the roadmap, and the ask. A launch social set, wide and square and tall, in one working file, because the date will move and the featured feature will move with it. Name badges for the fourteen people working the booth, each with their own photograph, ready for the badge printer. And the type we are on, written down.

Everything has to stay editable by us. We change pricing every quarter and we cannot come back to you each time.

Our tiers are twenty nine, seventy nine and two hundred forty nine dollars per seat, and enterprise annual runs near eighteen thousand. Our buyer is an IT or operations lead, thirty to fifty, at a company that signs annual contracts. It should look like software you would put your name on in front of a finance director: confident, evidence first, not loud. Tell us anything you could not do.
price_band_and_audience: Per seat tiers at 29, 79 and 249 dollars with enterprise annual near 18,000, sold to IT and operations leads aged 30 to 50 at 50 to 500 person firms who sign annual contracts and route the invoice past finance. The band is load-bearing rather than decorative. At this price the grammar has to be restrained and evidence led: generous white space, one accent, real numbers with their period stated, a tier table whose structure does the persuading, product screens shown honestly rather than dressed. Push it down into consumer app grammar, gradient bursts, cartoon mascots, exclamation copy and a tile packed to the edges, and the annual contract stops being credible to the person who has to defend the line item. Push it up into enterprise theatre, near black grounds, stock boardrooms, a wall of logos the company does not have, and an eleven person team in Denver reads as overstating itself to the exact buyer who will check. An agent can pass every technical gate and still misprice the work at either extreme. A real posted commission of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: B2B help desk software sold per seat to IT and operations leads at fifty to five hundred person firms.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Denver, Colorado, an eleven person team fourteen months into private beta.
brand_identity.about: Nimbadesk is help desk software for the internal IT and operations teams that keep mid sized companies running. We replace the tangle of shared inboxes and half configured legacy tools with one queue, clear ownership and reporting a director can actually read. We sell to the person who has to defend the line item, so everything we show is real: real screens, real numbers, real periods.
brand_identity.audience: IT and operations leads aged thirty to fifty at fifty to five hundred person firms who sign annual contracts and route the invoice past a finance director. They evaluate carefully, compare tiers before reading copy, and distrust hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Per seat tiers at 29, 79 and 249 dollars, with enterprise annual near 18,000. Mid market: above the free consumer tools, well below the enterprise suites, priced to be defended rather than impulse bought.
brand_identity.typography: A calm geometric sans for display, set tight at a real hierarchy, paired with a highly legible neutral sans for body and a tabular numeric face for metrics and the tier table. The feel is engineered and quiet, never showy.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, specific, understated. Numbers carry the argument and every claim states its period. Example line the brand would write: "Thirty one teams moved their queue to Nimbadesk this year. Here is what changed, and over what window."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No source files exist. The mark was generated by our first designer with an AI tool and delivered only as a flat picture, which is the single copy anywhere. There is no vector, no guideline document and no defined weight. Screenshots were captured ad hoc across the year at whatever scale the display was set to.
brand_identity.values: Evidence over theatre, and software a finance director would sign off without flinching.

assets_supplied.name: nimbadesk_ui_captures/ (11 PNG screen captures)
assets_supplied.kind: Product interface captures taken across roughly a year by whoever was at a keyboard, at whatever the display was set to.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have of the product. Some are newer than others."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the eleven were captured on a low resolution laptop display at roughly half the pixel scale of the rest, so bringing them to a common device treatment means enlargement, which the crop tool will perform silently up to a two times cap and report only inside its returned tradeoff record. Separately, two captures show the same feature at two different builds, one carrying a sidebar that no longer exists, and nothing in the filenames or the ordering says which is current.

assets_supplied.name: nimbadesk_logo_v4.png
assets_supplied.kind: The company mark as a raster picture, generated by the first designer with an AI tool: a monoline glyph inside a rounded badge, over a soft two stop gradient.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our logo. This picture is the only version that exists, the source file was never sent to us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The gradient means a trace returns dozens of near identical fills rather than a flat mark, and the fine glyph counters that read cleanly at canvas size close up at the size the mark actually reproduces at in a footer and on a badge. The file also carries a faint off white halo that is opaque rather than transparent, and any trace arrives with a full canvas ground rectangle and no viewBox.

assets_supplied.name: booth_headshots/ (14 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Headshots of the booth team taken in the office across two days against two different walls.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The fourteen people working the booth. Two different afternoons, whoever was free."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One person is present twice under two filenames while another on the roster has no frame at all, which the file count conceals because fourteen files exist. Several sitters wear pale shirts against the paler of the two walls, so subject detection has almost no contrast at the shoulder and hands back a soft rim on those frames alone.

assets_supplied.name: nimbadesk_badge_2026.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The badge printer's own artwork for the conference badge, four by three inches, with a photo well, a name line, a role line and the company line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The printer's badge file. They want one page per person back."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What prints as a neat square photo well is not what the converted document exposes: the picture frame's true bounds are portrait and inset under the type block, and the three type lines that print as three separate lines sit in one continuous story. Neither fact is visible on the printed page.

assets_supplied.name: nimbadesk_metrics.csv and nimbadesk_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The three headline numbers the chief executive wants charted, plus approved product copy, tier pricing, the roadmap lines and the fourteen person booth roster.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The numbers and the copy as approved. The tier prices are final for this quarter."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three headline figures are drawn from different periods, one from a ninety day pilot with six accounts and two from the full beta year, and no column in the file states any period.

acceptance_bar: Every product capture placed in the collateral is from the current build, shown at one device treatment and one scale logic, and no placed capture exceeds its source pixel dimensions or reaches its size by enlargement.
Where the same feature exists at two builds, one is chosen and the other is named in the note. A sheet never shows two versions of the same screen.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent ground, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as the same mark at the smallest size it actually reproduces at, on the dark ground as well as the light one.
In every delivered document the mark is live vector geometry and every word is text the client can retype, not a picture of a layout.
The three sell sheets, the deck and the social set carry one type system, one palette and one grammar. A reader who sees them a week apart sees one product.
The social set is ONE working file carrying all three canvases, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered together with the self contained source it was built from.
The tier table is a real table with per cell structure, and the recommended tier still reads as recommended in the delivered document, not only in the source it was built from.
The metrics chart is editable vector geometry, and every figure on it is labelled with the period it actually covers.

Fourteen badges, one page per person, each carrying that person's own photograph, with faces sitting the same way inside the frame across all fourteen, at true press resolution rather than screen resolution.
No person appears twice and nobody working the booth is missing. Any gap is named rather than filled with a stand in.

The note records the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight used, every resize any tool reported, the build version decisions, the period behind each metric, and anything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, counting image_vectorize HERE rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the engagement. It brings eleven captures taken at different display scales to one device treatment without enlargement, brings fourteen headshots shot on two walls across two days to one look and one cut, cuts the badge photo plates to the frame the document actually has, and recovers the mark from a gradient raster by flattening it to a plate before tracing rather than tracing the gradient, then performs the vector hygiene the tracing tool never does.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The sell sheets at true letter dimensions, the seven root deck with its chart, comparison and tier table, and the three canvas launch set as one document. This is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout, and it is the only one that returns an editable document the client can change next quarter. Every capture and headshot must be pulled down and embedded as image data because a URL renders as an empty box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because embedded photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed type system across sheets, deck, social set and the badge brief. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on credible mid market software rather than consumer app or enterprise theatre. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, display cuts are reached by their own slug, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with an @ prefixed image column and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The fourteen booth badges as a genuine record per page run built from the printer's own PDF, with each person's prepared headshot bound through the image column rather than one static picture repeated. It is also the only surface here that yields a real press resolution file, since the authoring surface returns an editable document and no exported file at all.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, orientation never passed), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the company does not have, an unstyled working environment band for the deck close and the wide launch canvas, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shortlist the founders sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable belongs on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The sheets, deck and social set need free form fixed canvas authoring and must stay editable, so they belong on the authoring surface. The badges need one page per person at press resolution, which only the layout and merge surface produces. The brief already pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable, plus the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which capture and which headshot belongs to which name on the roster.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and by roster name.

trajectory.action: Preview all eleven captures and all fourteen headshots and triage them: capture scale, interface build, chrome and crop, then read every headshot against the fourteen names on the roster.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts a year of captures and fourteen headshots. The pictures are the only thing that can settle which build each capture shows and whether fourteen files is fourteen people. Counting files is faster than reading faces against a roster and is not the same act.
trajectory.produces: A per file triage note covering capture scale, build version, wall and lighting, and a roster reconciliation naming any duplicate and any gap.

trajectory.action: Bring the captures to one device treatment at one scale logic, reading the returned tradeoff record on every crop rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff record is the only channel that says what happened to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. A capture that reaches the common treatment by being enlarged is a soft screenshot of software, which is the one thing this buyer inspects.
trajectory.produces: A consistent capture set with each frame's returned tradeoff record transcribed.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target from the best lit headshot and bring the other frames toward it one call at a time, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: Two walls across two days is two illuminants, so one batched identical parameter set is exactly the wrong instrument. The target is a set that reads as one team, not fourteen good portraits.
trajectory.produces: Graded portrait masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Knock the headshots onto the house ground, looking at each cut edge at full resolution rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: Pale shirt against pale wall gives subject detection almost nothing to hold at the shoulder, and that failure looks perfectly clean until the plate sits on a coloured ground. Where the one call route bites, the material named selection inverted and filled is the alternative.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen knocked out portrait plates with the route used recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Cut the badge photo plates so every face sits the same way inside the frame the badge actually carries.
trajectory.judgement: Faces sitting at different heights across fourteen badges is the failure a conference organiser notices from across a table, and consistency here is a crop logic decision rather than a per frame one.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen badge plates named to the roster.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark: reduce the gradient badge to a flat plate before tracing rather than tracing the gradient, choose the polarity, crop from the selection's own returned bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox and remove the full canvas ground path.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the mark and not the substrate, which polarity to trace, and whether the flattened plate or the colour accurate plate is the deliverable. The tracing tool takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a reverse variant for dark grounds.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull each family's style inventory for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical PostScript form, and build one kit for the whole system.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 29 to 249 dollar per seat band and a buyer who defends the line item to finance. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug, not by a heavier weight.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download the working environment frame at full resolution, then create the founders' shortlist board within the placement cap.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house target rather than the prettiest thumbnail, and remember a 201 response is partial success, not an error.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame and a persistent shortlist board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Author the three sell sheets as three roots at true letter dimensions in absolute units, embedding every capture as image data, placing the mark as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and declaring family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: The sheet is a sales instrument: header, the advantage the buyer is actually buying, the service bullets and one prominent call to action on a clean grid. How much air the band carries is the design decision, and restraint is the correct answer at this price.
trajectory.produces: One self contained HTML carrying the three sheets, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the file and export by URL, then verify through both channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per root markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at sheet one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document for the sheets, plus an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the others.

trajectory.action: Author the seven root deck on the same system: problem, product, the metrics as inline SVG geometry with each figure labelled by its period, how teams work today, the three tiers as a real table, the roadmap and the ask.
trajectory.judgement: Three figures from three different periods on one chart is a credibility problem, not a layout problem, and the honest treatments are to label or to drop. The tier table has to persuade by structure, since this reader compares rows before reading copy.
trajectory.produces: One HTML carrying the deck, with the metric periods resolved and recorded.

trajectory.action: Author the launch social set as three roots at three canvas sizes in one file, let each root declare its own canvas, then run the readiness check and export the deck and the set, auditing every root from the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: A global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set, so the sizes stay in the HTML. The set has to survive the featured feature and the date changing, which is a structural decision about where the variable copy sits.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document per piece, each with its per root markup audit.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's badge PDF, export the round tripped document structure, and read the true frame inventory before promising any field mapping.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed page looks like is not evidence of what the converted document contains. Frame granularity is not under the agent's control, and the inventory is the only honest basis for a mapping.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with real bounds, applied type and object styles per frame.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the true story text, prepare the merge template with the roster CSV and its image column, then verify by round tripping the document and confirming every placeholder actually landed.
trajectory.judgement: A successful preparation message is not evidence that a mapping landed, and the validator will report a mapping valid whether or not its offsets point where the agent thinks they do. The verification is the evidence.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present, and a roster CSV whose image column names the prepared plates.

trajectory.action: Merge one record and look at it, then merge the roster and render the press files at true press resolution, naming each output to the person it belongs to.
trajectory.judgement: One record inspected before fourteen is the cheapest possible insurance. Multi record raster labels cannot be trusted for identity, so the safe routes are the ordered file or one record per call.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen badge pages at press resolution, each identified to a named person.

trajectory.action: Write the note: type system by role, every resize any tool reported, the build version decisions, the metric periods, the roster reconciliation, and what could not be delivered.
trajectory.judgement: The note is a deliverable, not a receipt. It has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology, and honest about the limits, including that the editable documents cannot be exported to a file from that surface.
trajectory.produces: The written handover accompanying every file.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it actually reproduces at, on the ground it actually sits on. The trace is made from a gradient raster, so it comes back as dozens of near identical fills rather than a flat mark, and at canvas size it looks correct and complete. Placed at footer size on the sheet's house ground and exported, the fine glyph counters close up and the gradient bands into visible steps. Nothing in any tool response reports this: the trace has no options, no quality readout and no size advice, and the export reports success throughout. The only way to know is to look at the mark at its real reproduction size on the real ground after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because reproduction size only exists once the mark is placed and the placement only exists after the export, and the tracing tool exposes no parameter that would let an agent get it right in advance. Nothing in the brief states it, since the client says only that the picture is the only version that exists. The response is a different raster route rather than a re run: flatten the badge to a single value plate and trace that, or split the glyph from its container and rebuild the lockup, which is a different chain of calls with a different output.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging surface, prepare a flat plate instead of the gradient, retrace, redo the viewBox and ground path hygiene, produce a small size variant with opened counters and a reverse variant, then re author and re export every piece that carries the mark.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A company whose only surviving mark is shipped as a muddy blot in every footer and on fourteen badges, on collateral whose whole argument is that this is software you would put your name on.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construction that makes the recommended tier read as recommended. Authored the natural way, the middle tier card is lifted off the table with a layered shadow and a soft translucent panel behind it. The importer truncates a layered shadow to its first layer and drops the translucent treatment entirely, keeping only the flat fill underneath, and reports success with no warning. The tier table sits on deck root five, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so the returned per root markup is the sole channel in which the loss is visible at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The drop happens at import, which is the last step, so no ordering precedes it, and getting it right first time would require knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing in the brief or the deliverable list states it, since the client asks only for a table people can read. The response is a different construction, carrying emphasis in structure, weight, rule and scale rather than in depth effects, which changes the design rather than repeating it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cast the emphasis into constructions the importer preserves, re author the table and the tier cards, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A pitch deck in which the tier the company most wants sold sits visually level with the other two, delivered as an editable document that reported success at every step, in front of an investor audience and a buyer who compares rows.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the badge PDF actually becomes once converted. The printed badge shows a square photo well above three tidy type lines. The converted document does not have to match that: the picture frame's true bounds can be portrait and inset, and the three lines can sit in one continuous story rather than three mappable frames, in which case fields must be placed by position inside a single story instead of by frame. On top of that, the readout of that story can omit a run while keeping its line break, so every offset past the omission is short, and the mapping still reports as valid and the template preparation still reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity is a property of the conversion, not a choice, and nothing about the printed page predicts it, so no ordering and no care can establish it without converting and inspecting. The brief states only that the printer wants one page per person. The response is not a re run: it is a different mapping strategy computed against the true story text and a re cut of all fourteen photo plates to the frame that actually exists, which is upstream imaging work rather than a repeated merge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the true story text, re prepare and re verify the placeholders, return to the imaging surface to re cut every badge plate to the real frame ratio so faces still sit the same way, then re merge and re render.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen badges going to a printer with two fields blank or shifted and every face cropped differently by a frame nobody looked at, discovered at a conference booth where nothing can be reprinted.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need free form fixed canvas authoring and which need the one surface that yields a press resolution file, given that neither can do the other's job.
Which of two captures of the same feature is the current build, and how to say so when the client believes both are theirs.
Whether a capture can join the common device treatment at all, or has to be replaced or dropped rather than enlarged.
Knockout route per portrait: the one call route for sitters who separate from the wall, against a material named selection inverted and filled where shirt and wall run to the same value.
Whether the mark is recoverable as a flat plate trace, a colour accurate plate, or a rebuilt lockup, judged at reproduction size rather than at canvas size.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a per seat band defended to a finance director, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How to present three headline figures drawn from three different periods without either misleading the investor or gutting the chart.
How much air the sheets and deck carry. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit stuffed tile is a correct looking wrong answer.
Whether the fourteen files are fourteen people, and how to report a duplicate and a missing sitter rather than quietly shipping thirteen.
Field mapping strategy for the badge, which depends entirely on what the conversion exposes rather than on what the printed badge shows.
Which merge delivery route guarantees that the right badge carries the right name, given that positional labelling on raster output cannot be trusted for identity.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns handsome pictures of SaaS collateral. IDENTITY: these are this product's real interface screens and these fourteen are real people whose badges go round their necks, and the mark must be recovered from the only file that exists rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is another company's logo. SPEC: fourteen pages, one per roster name, each carrying that person's own photograph at press resolution from the printer's own artwork, and three social canvases at three exact sizes inside one file, none of which a generated image satisfies or can even be checked for. EDITABILITY: the whole engagement is defined by the client changing pricing every quarter without coming back, so a flat raster of a tier table is worthless to them. And the middle of the work is verification against material reality: does this mark still read at footer size, did the emphasis survive the import, is this frame the shape the printed badge implied.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); five honestly counted surfaces, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls; crop_and_resize is documented to upscale silently to a two times cap with the tradeoffs array as the only signal, and vectorize takes no options at all so a colour plate returns dozens of near identical fills, which is exactly the mark checkpoint. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, real tables with per cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG as native editable vector, exact letter canvases from absolute units, and a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search are all verified; multi layer box shadow is documented as a hard truncation to layer one and backdrop filter as dropped, both at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why the tier checkpoint can only be caught in the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because embedded photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold immediately, and no photograph is ever left as a URL. FONTS: recommend once per role, styles for the non standard numeric weights, find_fonts laundering and one kit are verified end to end, including a browser proving licensed faces load. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with an @ prefixed image column plus additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout at 300 DPI are all verified synchronous and headless, with frame granularity documented as not under the caller's control and textContent documented as lossy while the validator still reports valid. Delivery uses the ordered routes only, since multi record raster labels are documented as reversed. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 frame, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no text to image, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no bleed claim on a PDF derived template, no batch above 20, and no claim of a file export out of Express.
